newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA CENTRAL BANK PROBES INTERNAL ACCOUNTING.
newsitem.headline: CHINA CENTRAL BANK PROBES INTERNAL ACCOUNTING.

text.p: China's central bank has launched an investigation of accounting work in its subsidiaries as part of a nationwide campaign to clean up the fraud-ridden accounting industry, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.

The probe by the People's Bank of China was to ascertain whether its branches and local offices followed all accounting rules, including those concerning clearing and internal supervision, the newspaper said.
The investigation would be completed by the end of August, the newspaper said but gave no further details.

Beijing recently launched a crackdown on the nation's fledging accounting industry, with the Ministry of Finance conducting spot-checks of nearly 840,000 accounting offices, the official Xinhua news agency reported on Wednesday.
Of the offices checked, 16 percent held false accounts containing more than 14 billion yuan, it said.
The ministry fined 70,000 offices, disqualified more than 200 accountants, and filed charges against 46, Xinhua said.
Major offences included false accounts, fabricating information and keeping disorderly accounts, Xinhua quoted a ministry official as saying.
